transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jamal Rivera (CTO, Aurora), Sofia Gomez (Lead ML Eng), Lena Park (Security)

Summary: discovery call focused on migration from OpenAI-hosted usage to Redwood Dedicated / Private options. Main concerns: eval parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, compatibility with existing vLLM/TGI runners, network/compliance (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and pilot timeline. Agreed next steps and action items at end.

[00:00] Marcus Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Marcus from Redwood. Quick intros, then Priya will jump into technical questions.
[00:15] Jamal Rivera: Hey Marcus, Jamal here. We run Aurora's customer support assistant and a few embeddings pipelines; currently most calls go through OpenAI but we've started spinning up vLLM for internal cost tests.
[00:30] Marcus Lee: Great, can you give us a quick snapshot of volume and what you're hoping to get out of Dedicated or Private?
[00:42] Sofia Gomez: Yeah, sure. Right now about 1.5M tokens/day, spiky traffic (weekdays peak), avg latency target for chat paths is <250ms token-latency if possible. Main drivers: reduce per-token cost, keep PII in our VPC, and avoid throttles we've seen from our current provider.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Thanks, that's helpful. A few clarifying questions: when you say vLLM, are you running it in prod or just experiments? Which model families do you rely on from OpenAI today (gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, etc.)?
[01:20] Sofia Gomez: We have a prod vLLM for embeddings and some generative experiments, but most prod traffic still hits OpenAI gpt-4o-like endpoint for critical user flows. We're testing TGI for some workloads.
[01:35] Jamal Rivera: Also want to confirm: we're evaluating Dedicated to get predictable throughput and potentially a Private deployment later for data residency.
[01:50] Marcus Lee: Makes sense. At a high level, Dedicated gets you reserved GPU pools with SLOs and isolation; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and on-prem options. Both support model variants in our catalog.
[02:05] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) how does model parity look vs OpenAI?
[02:12] Priya Nair: Good question — we do model verification during onboarding. For OpenAI parity we run evals on your prompt set to compare output quality and token cost. For large models there can be small differences due to tokenizer or model weights; we aim for functional parity and tune prompts or recommend compatible model variants.
[02:38] Sofia Gomez: And what about vLLM/TGI compatibility? Our infra team already has TGI and vLLM in the stack, we want to avoid redoing evaluation work if we move.
[02:50] Priya Nair: Redwood's runtime can serve most open model formats; we integrate with common backends and we can run the same model binaries where practical. For TGI/vLLM-specific optimizations, we sometimes recommend quantized builds or slightly different kernel paths; Priya pauses, sorry — I mean, we have a migration checklist to minimize rework.
[03:12] Jamal Rivera: Any gotchas around KV cache and conversation state when switching runtimes? We rely heavily on long-context chat.
[03:24] Priya Nair: We support KV cache and we maintain session-level cache semantics; there can be differences in incremental generation speed depending on quantization and hardware, but our profiling during pilot captures token latency and end-to-end response times.
[03:40] Lena Park: From security side: SOC2, SSO, KMS, and audit logs are must-haves. Also need to know about private connectivity — can Redwood Dedicated be placed inside our VPC or use private link?
[03:55] Marcus Lee: Short answer: yes. Dedicated supports private connectivity options (VPC peering, private link patterns) and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane. We have KMS integrations and HSM options for Private, and we provide audit logs per request. We'll share the security whitepaper after this call.
[04:15] Sofia Gomez: Are you supporting Anthropic models or only open models? Some of our teams like Claude family for safety differences.
[04:25] Priya Nair: We work with multiple families; hosted catalog includes vetted open weights and we have verified performance profiles. For Anthropic models, there are licensing considerations — we can discuss specifics in the legal/security review, but we can route to compatible behavior or run an Anthropic-hosted endpoint depending on the contract.
[04:45] Jamal Rivera: Cost: can you ballpark savings vs OpenAI if we run Dedicated? We have current unit cost around $0.12 per 1k tokens for completion — rough numbers are fine.
[05:00] Marcus Lee: Ballpark only: Dedicated can drop unit costs substantially for sustained volume because of reserved capacity + quantization and batching; typical customers see 30-60% drop depending on model and sequence lengths. We'll produce a modeled estimate once we see your traffic histogram.
[05:20] Sofia Gomez: Good. For our evals we care about both quality (ROUGE/BLEU/LLM-eval metrics) and hallucination rates on our domain prompts.
[05:30] Priya Nair: We'll run the eval parity plan — compare outputs side-by-side, measure latency, tokens, and cost, and flag any regression. If we find a quality gap, we either recommend a different model in our catalog or adjust prompts/temperature.
[05:45] Speaker 2: (soft) timeline question — our procurement window is end of Q1.
[05:50] Marcus Lee: That aligns well; pilot in December/January could feed procurement for Q1.
[06:00] Jamal Rivera: For the pilot, what does Redwood need from us?
[06:05] Priya Nair: Primarily: sample prompts (Sofia), traffic profile and spikes (Sofia), security requirements and network diagram (Lena), and a list of use cases and success metrics (Jamal). We'll set up a benchmarking harness and run your prompts vs OpenAI + vLLM baseline.
[06:25] Sofia Gomez: On the vLLM baseline: we run a GPU cluster with vLLM using a quantized Llama variant for embeddings and a mixture of Llama/OPT for generative tasks. Will Redwood be able to reproduce that exact config?
[06:40] Priya Nair: We can often reproduce model binaries if they're open; for proprietary forks we may need to run equivalence tests. We focus on delivering comparable latency/cost and maintaining tokenization equivalence. If you provide Docker images or model artifacts, our SE team can evaluate.
[06:58] Marcus Lee: Quick note on tooling: Redwood Console has per-route latency and token breakdowns, and you can do canary rollouts so you can measure regressions on a small subset before full cutover.
[07:12] Lena Park: Do you log user prompts? We need to ensure PII is not stored unless encrypted and controlled by our KMS.
[07:22] Marcus Lee: By default, Redwood does not retain customer prompts longer than necessary; for Private deployments you control retention and KMS. We'll add the retention policy docs.
[07:35] Sofia Gomez: Any limitations around streaming responses and function calling? We use function calls extensively for structured tool orchestration.
[07:45] Priya Nair: We support streaming and function/tool calling. A few models have different function-calling semantics, but we support structured output and webhooks.
[07:58] Jamal Rivera: What about autoscaling and burst capacity during peak events? Our site has big spikes after product launches.
[08:06] Marcus Lee: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst pools; we can set burst policies for N minutes to handle transient spikes. For Private, you'd manage autoscaling but we can provide policies and tooling.
[08:20] Speaker 3: (muffled) can you do inference on bare metal?
[08:25] Priya Nair: For Private on-prem deployments, yes, but there are capacity planning and ops requirements; we'll coordinate with your infra team.
[08:35] Sofia Gomez: For eval parity, can you include token-level latency distribution and tail latency (p95/p99)? Those are important.
[08:43] Priya Nair: Absolutely, we'll capture p50/p95/p99 plus cost per token, also effective throughput under batching.
[08:55] Marcus Lee: Ok, let's walk through an example pilot plan.
[09:00] Priya Nair: Step 1: onboarding + security vetting (week 1). Step 2: run bench harness with your sample prompts across OpenAI, vLLM baseline, and Redwood Dedicated config (week 2). Step 3: analyze outputs, check eval parity, adjust models (week 3). Step 4: small canary in production for 1-2 weeks, then roll.
[09:25] Jamal Rivera: Sounds reasonable. What's the minimum committed capacity for Dedicated?
[09:30] Marcus Lee: Depends on GPU type; we have starter plans for smaller pools but typical enterprise commitments start at monthly reserved nodes. We'll include options in the pricing doc.
[09:42] Sofia Gomez: Any regulatory concerns for EU data residency? We have customers in EU and need data to stay within region.
[09:50] Marcus Lee: We have region-aware routing and Private deployments can be run in EU regions; Dedicated can be provisioned in specific regions depending on capacity.
[10:00] Lena Park: A few follow-ups for security: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC granularity, request-level audit logs, and encryption at rest with our KMS.
[10:12] Marcus Lee: We'll include details for each and a checklist in the security packet.
[10:20] Sofia Gomez: Ok, any cost estimate for the pilot? Even rough.
[10:25] Marcus Lee: For a short pilot, we can do a time-limited evaluation using our hosted infra to simulate Dedicated performance; cost is modest and we'll credit it if you move forward. Exact numbers in proposal.
[10:40] Jamal Rivera: One more question: we use a downstream retriever and embeddings store. Does Redwood have an embeddings endpoint compatible with our vector DB (we use Milvus/FAISS)?
[10:52] Priya Nair: Yes, we provide embeddings APIs that return standard vectors; most customers plug those into Milvus/FAISS. We'll verify dimensionality with your model choices.
[11:05] Speaker 1: (short) any legal docs in advance?
[11:08] Marcus Lee: We'll share a redlined MSA template and typical timelines for procurement.
[11:12] Closing minutes
[11:12] Marcus Lee: Recap: Marcus to send pricing + security docs; Priya to prepare benchmark plan; Aurora to provide prompts and traffic hist; schedule follow-up technical deep dive next week. Anything else?
[11:28] Sofia Gomez: No, that's it. Thanks.
[11:32] Jamal Rivera: Thanks everyone.
[11:40] End of call.

Notes about transcript: There are minor transcription artifacts (speaker mislabels and small word swaps). The technical content captured includes KV cache, quantization, batching, region routing, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, SOC2, eval parity benchmarking vs OpenAI and vLLM/TGI, Dedicated autoscaling and burst policies, and Private deployment options.
